request.spec:
Show for the sheet the due of OPEN and PENDING claims that count by age, as the people's age
buckets added up (0 to 30, 31 to 60, 61 or more days), not trimmed.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Show for the sheet the due of OPEN and PENDING claims that count by age, as the people's age
buckets added up (0 to 30, 31 to 60, 61 or more days), not trimmed.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The sheet now shows its own age buckets, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests.

The only file changed is `src/main/frontend/features/aging/aging.slot.tsx`:

- **What it shows:** a new line on the sheet, placed just after "Cuts in total", reading "Due by age: 0–30 days X, 31–60 days Y, 61+ days Z". The three figures carry `rollup-aged-0-30`, `rollup-aged-31-60` and `rollup-aged-61`, the test IDs the spec expects.
- **How it adds up:** each figure is every person's bucket for that age range added together, with no cap applied. Each person's buckets are worked out exactly as the existing per-person columns are: OPEN and PENDING claims that count, sorted by the claim's age on the sheet's today. I moved that calculation into a shared helper so the per-person columns and the sheet totals can't drift apart. The per-person columns look the same as before.

No server, stored-data or audit changes were needed: the spec expects no new audit records, and everything the totals need is already on the page.
